claims.text: Large language models are trained on internet corpora that often include inaccurate or misleading content.
Large language models can generate misinformation.
Current evaluation metrics for LLM factuality have limitations.
Domain-specific customization improves the factual consistency of large language models.
Validated external evidence is essential for evaluating and maintaining factual accuracy in LLMs.

evidence.description: LLMs are trained on vast and diverse internet corpora that often include inaccurate or misleading content.
Consequently, LLMs can generate misinformation, making robust fact-checking essential.
The key findings demonstrate the limitations of current metrics in factuality evaluation.
The review demonstrates the improvement of factual consistency through domain-specific customization.
Key findings highlight the importance of validated external evidence for LLM factual accuracy.

methodologies.name: Systematic Literature Review
methodologies.description: Systematic analysis of recent literature from 2020 to 2025 guided by five research questions on LLM evaluation methods and mitigation techniques.

limitations.text: Current metrics for factual accuracy evaluation in LLMs have limitations.
Internet corpora used for training LLMs often contain inaccurate or misleading content.

future_work.text: Developing more accurate, understandable, and context-aware fact-checking frameworks.
